rows.description: A young child learns that waiting for a turn at the slide or counter is expected. They feel impatient and rely on adult praise and a clear sense of fairness to hold on.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child pushes ahead because they are in a hurry or think no one will mind. They feel a flash of guilt or defiance depending on how others react.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A parent thanks the bus conductor, waits patiently in line and apologises for a bump. Children learn public manners far more from watching than from being told.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: Teenagers laugh loudly on a bus or in a cinema, enjoying their group's energy and forgetting others. It is usually thoughtlessness, and a calm word often corrects it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Queue jumped by a well-connected person [Receiver]
rows.description: A person waiting patiently sees someone with influence walk to the front. They feel anger and helplessness, and the sight teaches some to accept unfairness and others to object.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Giving up a seat or space [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult offers their seat or gives way to an elderly person or a pregnant woman. The small act comes from awareness of others and needs no praise.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A commuter sees someone jump a queue or litter and wonders whether to speak. They weigh safety and tone, and often a light, polite comment works better than a scolding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: curiosity, awe, trust

rows.description: A person says excuse me, the line starts there, without heat. Calm, friendly firmness usually works, and if it turns hostile they let it go.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child cheers for a cricket team or film hero and wears the colours proudly. Loving the same thing as others gives instant belonging and a story to be part of.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager's music, series or team becomes part of who they are. They feel understood by other fans and defensive when their idol is criticised, as though the criticism were personal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
